title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: S&P 500, Nasdaq and Dow all snapped a three-day losing streak Wednesday (+0.46%, +0.45%, +0.56%) as stocks shrugged off Mideast tensions; Thursday futures are flat-to-lower ahead of Friday's jobs report.

Markets: Oil spiked on renewed US-Iran fighting near the Strait of Hormuz — Brent above $95/bbl, WTI near $91 — as vessel crossings through the strait dropped sharply, reviving supply-disruption fears.
Markets: Gold rose to roughly $4,431/oz and the 10-year Treasury yield eased slightly, even as bond markets stay jittery over inflation risk from high oil prices.
Companies: Alphabet shares rose after a court declined to break up its ad-tech business, ordering behavioral fixes instead of the DOJ's requested breakup.
Companies: Uber is cutting 10% of its workforce to flatten management and reinvest, following a soft growth outlook in last month's earnings; the stock rose 1.6%.
Companies: Chevron will invest $7B in Venezuela over five years to double output to 600k bpd, the biggest post-Maduro bet by a major oil company.
Macro/Policy: Gasoline prices are on track for a Labor Day record above $4/gal, as the oil spike compounds a global diesel/refined-fuel crunch analysts call a distinct energy-security risk.
Macro/Policy: The Fed's next rate decision lands Sept 16; markets are watching Friday's August jobs report and next week's CPI print after the Fed held rates at 3.50-3.75% in July.

Macro/Policy: US data-center construction spending jumped ~60% YoY in July to a $75B+ annualized pace, underscoring continued AI capex acceleration even as political backlash grows and Anthropic/OpenAI jockey ahead of expected blockbuster IPOs.
